fields.System.Title: INV-8 — Reconciliation
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Check nightly that the ledger still explains the balances, alert when it does not, and be able
to rebuild balances from scratch when needed.

Scope

In. The ledger-vs-balance check, alerting, balance rebuild.

Out. Other reconciliations — projections
([INV-903](../../stories/INV/INV-903-reconcile-projection.md)), reservations
([INV-504](../../stories/INV/INV-504-report-orphaned-reservations.md)), and the ERP comparison
([INT-504](../../stories/INT/INT-504-ledger-balance-drift-report.md)).

Design notes

This feature is the system's core promise, made checkable.

Everything rests on one invariant: every balance change wrote a movement. If it holds, balances
are rebuildable, history is complete, and any number can be explained. If it is broken even
occasionally, you cannot trust any number and you cannot tell which ones to distrust.

Treat a failure as a stop-everything incident, not a ticket. And do not auto-correct — a
discrepancy is a symptom, and correcting it hides the code path that caused it.

INV-802 is not optional. A check that finds drift and writes it to a log nobody reads is
not a control. It has to reach a human.

A note on go-live. If opening stock is loaded directly into balances without movements,
this job fails on day one, every night, and gets switched off — taking with it your ability to
detect the bug it exists for. Load opening stock as receipts against a GO-LIVE reason code.
See [doc 09 §11.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md).

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Drift found but not alerted | [doc 08 §9](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| Auto-correcting instead of investigating | [doc 08 §9](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| Opening stock loaded without movements | [doc 09 §11.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
